title: Cover and Protocol
premise: Odile Vasquez, a fixer for the Meridian Liaison Office—an embassy that exists on no map—has spent nine years keeping other people's secrets sealed and her own life disposable. When Flight 447's records vanish mid-flight while the plane is still airborne, she discovers the disappearance was engineered inside her own office to mask a cargo of nerve agent bound for a 'controlled' demolition in the city. Betrayed by the mentor who trained her and shadowed by an inspector who should be her enemy, Odile must choose between the protocol that made her and the truth that could burn everyone she's protected. In the end she stops the attack minutes before dawn, burns the office's black ledger rather than hand it to any government, and walks away from the extraction flight—alive, disavowed, and finally free.
about_author: Ivo Sandoval is the pen name of a former diplomatic security contractor who writes thrillers from a rotating series of rented apartments. His work is known for procedural precision, morally compromised institutions, and protagonists who are very good at leaving.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Odile Vasquez's POV. A routine night scrubbing a diplomat's indiscretion from three databases establishes her world: the Meridian Liaison Office, her polished lies, her packed bag by the door. Emotional beat: controlled competence masking a woman who owns nothing permanent.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She's assigned to 'soften' the paperwork on a charter flight before it lands. Mid-task, every record of the flight evaporates across every system while radar still shows it climbing. Emotional beat: the first crack—the professional unease of a lie she didn't write.

chapters.title: Ghost on the Scope
chapters.summary: Inspector Tomas Reiner's POV, introduced as he investigates the vanished flight from outside. He notices one anomaly: a fixer's credentials touched the file forty seconds before deletion. Emotional beat: cold curiosity hardening into pursuit.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Hand
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Her mentor, Director Casimir Hale, orders her to stand down and hands her a new identity and a dawn extraction slot. The kindness itself is the warning. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by the shape of the favor.

chapters.title: What the Cargo Manifest Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, breaking protocol. She pulls a cached fragment of the manifest: canisters mislabeled as industrial coolant, routed to a decommissioned waterworks downtown. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Reiner at the Door
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Reiner confronts Odile with the credential log; instead of arresting each other, they trade what they know over bad coffee. Uneasy alliance formed. Emotional beat: two professionals recognizing the same trap.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Sealed Rooms
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, flashback-woven. We learn how Hale recruited her out of a scandal she didn't commit, and why duty became her religion. Emotional beat: understanding what she stands to lose by turning.

chapters.title: The Waterworks
chapters.summary: Odile and Reiner scout the site at night: ventilation retrofitted, timers installed, a dispersal system aimed at the morning commuter flood. It's built to read as a gas main accident. Emotional beat: horror under fluorescent calm.

chapters.title: Deniable Assets
chapters.summary: Reiner's POV. He reports up his own chain and watches his report get buried within the hour—the rot isn't just Meridian. Emotional beat: an honest man learning his institution is a costume.

chapters.title: Hale's Lesson
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Hale catches her snooping but doesn't kill her; instead he explains the doctrine—thirty lives traded now against a war deterred later—and offers her the extraction seat as a partner. Emotional beat: seduction of the devil she loves.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She copies Meridian's black ledger—nine years of traded lives—including the entry that proves Flight 447 carried the agent deliberately. Emotional beat: grief and resolve fused; no way back.

chapters.title: Burn Notice, Reverse
chapters.summary: Reiner's POV. Meridian frames Reiner for the data wipe; his badge, accounts, and apartment unravel in real time. He goes dark and reaches Odile through their one shared dead-drop. Emotional beat: fugitive solidarity.

chapters.title: Countdown Logistics
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The pair maps the attack timeline against the dawn extraction: the device arms at 5:40, wheels-up at 6:15, and Meridian's cleaners arrive at 5:00 to erase loose ends—them. Emotional beat: ticking-clock compression.

chapters.title: The Cleaner
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Meridian sends Voss, the fixer who trained beside her, to retire her. A rooftop confrontation ends with Odile sparing her and Voss walking away—protocol broken twice in one night. Emotional beat: mercy as rebellion.

chapters.title: Inside the Perimeter
chapters.summary: Reiner's POV. Using his still-valid forensic access, Reiner talks them past the waterworks' private security, but the entry logs a breach they can't undo. Emotional beat: the point of no return crossed knowingly.

chapters.title: Wiring and Doubt
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, alone in the pump gallery. She finds the timer rigged with a fail-deadly anti-tamper loop and realizes disarming requires someone to hold the circuit manually. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into arithmetic—who holds the wire.

chapters.title: Hale Arrives
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Hale appears at the site, not with cleaners but alone, offering one last trade: walk to the plane, and the city's near-miss becomes a lesson learned. Odile asks him to say the victims' names. He can't. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided.

chapters.title: Dawn Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She triggers the tamper loop deliberately, forcing the device onto a manual hold, and wires herself to it while Reiner races to reroute the dispersal lines. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen without melodrama.

chapters.title: Five Forty-One
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. Reiner vents the agent harmlessly skyward as sirens rise; Odile, guided by Reiner's voice, cuts the last relay with ninety seconds left. Hale, watching from the perimeter, makes a call on his phone—and lets her live. Emotional beat: breath released after held tension.

chapters.title: The Extraction Gate
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the airfield, the dawn flight waits with her name on the manifest and Hale waiting at the stairs—not to stop her, but to ask. She gives him the ledger's location encrypted and unopenable, boards nothing. Emotional beat: farewell without hatred.

chapters.title: Disavowed
chapters.summary: Reiner's POV. Officially, the waterworks incident was a gas main failure; officially, Inspector Reiner resigned. He meets Odile at a train platform where neither uses a real name. Emotional beat: justice achieved outside the law, paid for in identity.

chapters.title: New Bag, Empty Pocket
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, epilogue. Somewhere south, she packs a go-bag again—but this time it's hers, holding nothing anyone ordered her to carry. A postcard arrives with no signature, only a flight number that never existed. Emotional beat: freedom as an open road, vigilance as habit.
